conventions.convention: The action uses a finite interval [a,b] with a<b, an open nonempty configuration domain U, a C² Lagrangian on an open domain containing [a,b]×U×Rⁿ, and C² curves admitting extensions to an open interval. Variations vanish at both endpoints.
The Euler–Lagrange expression is L_q−d(L_v)/dt; stationarity means vanishing first variation, without a minimum claim.
Regularity means a nonsingular velocity Hessian. Hyperregularity requires bijectivity onto each full momentum fibre and a jointly C¹ inverse assignment.
For holonomic constraints, virtual displacements satisfy G_qδ=0, permitted velocities satisfy G_t+G_qv=0, and the reaction sign is R=G_qᵀλ.

The holonomic acceleration and maximal-solution proposition assumes G∈C³, f∈C¹, constant symmetric positive definite M, and full rank G_q throughout the open domain. Constraint preservation requires both consistent position and consistent velocity.

For z′=xy′, allowed velocities and Chetaev virtual displacements are D(q)={w:w_z=xw_y}. d’Alembert motions satisfy q″⊥D(q); vakonomic motions use stationarity of the augmented functional with independently varied curve and multiplier.

The reparametrisation charge is C=p·ξ−Eτ−B, where E=p·v−L. Time translation with ξ=0, τ=1, B=0 gives minus the energy; the boost convention gives a·(tmp′−mq), with p′ here replaced by q′ in the stated charge a·(tmq′−mq).
Phase-action variations fix q endpoints and leave p endpoints free.

Endpoint action integrates from the fixed initial time t₀ to the variable endpoint time t, with oriented integrals when t<t₀, and assumes a selected C² family of extremals with fixed initial configuration.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the C² time-dependent Lagrangian chart, admissible curves and fixed-endpoint variations, action, first variation, stationarity, and E_L(q)=L_q−d(L_v)/dt.
For a chart, admissible C² curve q and variation η, q+εη remains admissible for sufficiently small ε; the action is differentiable in ε, δS(q)[η]=∫[L_q·η+L_v·η′]dt, and E_L(q) is continuous.
An admissible C² curve q is stationary for S if and only if E_L(q)(t)=0 for every t∈[a,b].
On a hyperregular C² fibre-full chart, H_p=v, H_q=−L_q and H_t=−L_t; a C¹ phase curve satisfies Hamilton’s equations iff q is C², E_L(q)=0 and p=L_v(t,q,q′); along these curves e=H and e′=−L_t.

For C³ full-rank G, constant symmetric positive definite M and C¹ f, the stated multiplier and acceleration are C¹ and give a unique maximal first-order solution through every datum. Consistent data preserve G=0 and G_t+G_qq′=0; the reaction power is −Λ·G_t, and ideal motions with permitted velocity are exactly consistent-data solutions.
If C² data τ, ξ and B satisfy L_tτ+L_q·ξ+L_v·(D_tξ−vD_tτ)+LD_tτ=D_tB on the chart, then p·ξ−(p·v−L)τ−B is constant along every stated C² Euler–Lagrange solution.
For C³ time-dependent X with invertible X_q and C² L, the substituted Lagrangian is C² and its Euler–Lagrange expression along q equals X_qᵀ times the ambient expression along x=X(t,q).
The Legendre derivative is invertible iff the velocity Hessian is nonsingular; a nonsingular velocity Hessian yields a local C¹ diffeomorphism.

concerns.concern: The second Remark says: “Multiple extremals through the same endpoint data, or a degenerating endpoint map, are exactly the situations in which no single-valued C² family exists”. Multiplicity does not prevent selecting a smooth branch. A concrete hyperregular example is L(q,v)=|v|²/(2|q|²) on U=R²\{0}: in local lifted coordinates ρ=log|q| and θ it is (ρ′²+θ′²)/2. With initial point (1,0), endpoint time t near 1 and endpoint q near (1,0), write α(q) for the smooth local angle. For every integer k, X_k(t,q,s)=exp(s log|q|/t)(cos(s(α(q)+2πk)/t),sin(s(α(q)+2πk)/t)) is a smooth family of extremals with the required endpoints. At t=1,q=(1,0), distinct winding extremals coexist with each selected smooth family. The theorem’s conditional Statement and proof do not require uniqueness and remain sound.

The Example introduces “a C² curve θ:I→Ω” without defining I; its Given block also leaves I undeclared. Clause 2 and step 2.1 conclude that energy is constant on I using a theorem requiring an interval. If I is a disconnected open time domain, different components can carry solutions with different energies. State explicitly that I is an open interval, as the reduced d’Alembert supplier requires.

The first Remark says “The bump of this lemma is a polynomial”. The bump is piecewise polynomial, equals zero on exterior open intervals, and equals one at c; therefore it cannot be a single polynomial on R. The explicit construction and C² gluing proof are sound.

The bundle-comparison Remark refers to “the explicit C² inverse branch on J×U×Rⁿ”. Hyperregularity in this Definition requires a C¹ inverse, and the local-invertibility lemma supplies C¹ for a C² Lagrangian. The stronger inverse regularity is not a general hypothesis or conclusion here.

alerts.finding: The Statement ends “Equivalently, the row vector of ℓ is Aᵀλ”. With A an n×m matrix and λ an n-component column, Aᵀλ is an m-component column. The coefficient column is Aᵀλ; the row is λᵀA. The preceding functional identity is correctly typed and is what the batch’s multiplier proof uses.

Definition (e) says the counterexample “proves that the unique d’Alembert motion is not vakonomic with those data”. The cited item proves uniqueness of the maximal motion and says every other motion through the datum is a restriction. Under the motion definition, restrictions to different open intervals are distinct motions, so “unique” needs “maximal” or a restriction/germ qualification.

The second paragraph says the counterexample “proves that the unique d’Alembert motion is not a vakonomic motion with those data”. The source distinguishes its unique maximal trajectory from its many interval restrictions. The non-vakonomic conclusion is supported; the uniqueness wording omits that qualification.

F1 cites prop-cm-ideal-holonomic-system-in-a-time-dependent-chart and restates its system correspondence and reaction-power conclusions “for a C² regular constraint”. The cited proposition states G∈C³ and f∈C¹. The example’s actual affine constraint and constant force satisfy the stronger hypotheses, but the cited general fact does not preserve the supplier’s regularity. A C²-only version would require its own stated local derivation.

Pendulum and hoop use the strict-minimum energy theorem with positive constant reduced mass and C² potentials; the critical hoop case is proved to be a strict minimum. The pendulum frequency uses the scalar positive-stiffness mode theorem. The pendulum’s undeclared I is separately recorded.
Multiplier balance preserves C³ G, C¹ force, rank and consistency hypotheses. Two nonholonomic summaries omit “maximal” from the cited uniqueness conclusion; both item alerts are recorded.

The pendulum multiplier use preserves the supplier hypotheses. Rolling-disk F1 weakens the cited proposition’s C³ constraint hypothesis to C², although its actual affine datum is smooth; an alert is recorded.

Point and general Noether uses retain the identity as a hypothesis, C² general generators, the charge sign p·ξ−Eτ−B and potential-branch restrictions. Moving-chart energy uses the stated hyperregular identity.
